fact: The World Bank mission found the Integrated Revenue Management System for Local Authorities (GIR-CT) operational at the national level, with its functions interfaced with local systems so municipalities manage the whole local taxation chain; verification of the result was still pending.

The World Bank status report says GIR-CT operationalisation is complete in more than 100 large municipalities (target of at least 100 large municipalities), still to be verified; it gives no total of municipalities.

The World Bank status report records the electronic declaration and payment system for municipal taxes as operational (indicator 6.3 achieved), against none at baseline, as of the August 2025 mission.
system: electronic declaration and payment system for municipal taxes

fact: The World Bank appraisal says the national treasury (TGR) had established and extended the Integrated Revenue Management System for local authorities (GIR-CT), and that new GIR-CT features covering the whole chain from tax base to recovery were to be made available to municipalities; the TGR collects all municipal revenues except the professional tax.

The Interior Ministry's circular n° 32 states the integrated revenue management platform GIR-CT was already deployed in 969 of 1,590 local authorities (collectivités territoriales), as of 19 May 2020.

The circular says the Walis and Governors steer revenue recovery through the GIR-Reporting system, and that the revenue offices (régies) of local authorities, including wholesale markets and abattoirs, are being dematerialised and integrated into the GIR-CT platform.

The circular, signed by the Minister of the Interior through the DGCT, directs authorising officers to equip their revenue offices with computers, printers, cheque readers and internet and to work with the Treasury (TGR) on the generalisation of GIR-CT.
